column3: NASB renders “call His name” as “name Him.”
Close to the Greek.
“To the ages” is rendered “forever.”
NASB renders “since I do not know a man” as “since I am a virgin.”
NASB renders “the holy one being born” as “the holy Child.”
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “even” and “now.”
NASB follows the critical text; “every word will not be impossible” is rendered “nothing will be impossible.”
“Handmaid” is rendered “bondslave”; “declaration” is “word.”
NASB renders “in these days” as “at this time” and “town” as “city.”
NASB spells “Zacharias.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text; “shout” is rendered “voice.”
NASB renders “from where to me this” as “how has it happened to me.”
“Voice” is rendered “sound,” and “in exultation” is “for joy.”
NASB renders “the one having believed” as “she who believed.” The Greek may also be read “because there will be a fulfillment.”
“Magnifies” is rendered “exalts.”
NASB renders the aorist “rejoiced” as “has rejoiced.”
NASB renders “humiliation” as “humble state” and “handmaiden” as “bondslave.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text (“generation after generation”); the line is in capitals as an Old Testament allusion.
“Shown strength” is rendered “done mighty deeds.”
NASB adds “their.”
Close to the Greek; the first line is in capitals.
“Remembering” is rendered “in remembrance of.”
“To the age” is rendered “forever.”
NASB adds “then.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “magnified His mercy” as “had displayed His great mercy.”
NASB follows the critical text; “were calling” is rendered “were going to call.”
NASB adds “indeed.”
